helpers.note: rounds an f64 to binary32 and widens it back, the engine's spelling of Java's (float) cast where a double carries a float value; a language cast, not a vanilla method
multiplies degrees by the float-rounded PI / 180 and rounds the product to float, the inline `f * ((float)Math.PI / 180F)` vanilla writes at its call sites; Mth has no degrees-to-radians method

the float sum x*x + z*z; Mth has no lengthSquared(float, float) (Mth.length(float, float) widens to the double overload, which length_2_f32 follows), so this float form mirrors no vanilla method and its test shows it rounding differently

the engine's refusal bound: false when the box would walk more than MAX_WALKED_CELLS cells or reaches past MAX_COORDINATE; vanilla walks any box, so the bindings' out-of-range refusal has no vanilla counterpart
an upper bound on the block cells a box spans, (size + 2) per axis multiplied, which feeds the engine's MAX_WALKED_CELLS refusal; vanilla has no such count
